questions.question: ________ is the smallest bone in the human body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Stapes__**.

 
• **Smallest Bone in the Human Body**

 
 
• At 3 mm x 2.5 mm, the "**stapes**" in the middle ear is the smallest named bone in the human body.
 
• The shape of a stirrup, this bone is one of three in the middle ear, collectively known as the ossicles.
 
• The ossicles convey sound pressure waves from the outer ear (and eardrum) to the inner ear, where the waves are translated into nerve impulses that go to the brain for identification.
 
• The other two ossicles are the malleus (hammer) and the incus (anvil).

questions.question: Which of the following are **NOT** a part of the circulatory system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Villi__**.

 
• **Capillaries** are called very **tiny blood vessels**.
 
• The **Capillaries** expand like a mesh in the whole body.
 
• Through **these capillaries, blood is transported** to all parts of the whole body.
 
• **The arteries **are the blood vessels that carry blood from the heart.
 
• **All arteries **carry **oxygen-rich blood, **except for pulmonary and avascular arteries.
 
• **A tube** that **carries blood** from the body to the heart and returns back is called a** 'vein'.**
 
• '**Villy' **is a structure found in the intestine that helps to **absorb nutrients from the food eaten.**
